title: The Secret of the Talking Mushrooms
markdown:
The sun came up like a golden pancake flipping over the hills. Pink and orange hit the sky in bright streaks. Fern the mushroom farmer stretched, a mighty yawn, toes finding the cool boards. A tickle at her nose said the day had already started without her. She padded to the window, bare feet quick.

Outside, her prize patch glittered. Dew on every velvety cap, a million small coins. Not ordinary wet: a curious light, as if the night had left stars in the grass.

Click-whirr. Skiff the tin owl bounced onto the sill, gear-eyes busy as kettles.

"Fern. Fern. You will not believe it. The mushrooms. They are talking."

She pushed a bouncy curl back. "Talking, Skiff. Your clever gears again."

"Listen." His metal ears perked.

She leaned. Breath caught. A rustle of a thousand tiny secrets, all at once. The Wishing Drizzle — the once-a-year rain that loosened mushroom tongues — had been through in the dark.

The mushrooms were talking.

"What are they saying?"

Skiff hopped down, tin buzzing. "That is the tricky part. A top secret. But one patch is louder than the rest. If they shout it out… sunset is not as far as it looks."

Fern's heart did a quick skip. She knew. Farmer Giles's birthday. Everyone in Willow Creek had been folding a surprise by the Big Old Oak: quiet plans, louder cake, balloons kept in sheds. If the King Boletes blabbed before dusk, the surprise would arrive as a rumour with a crown-cap.

"We keep it," she said, clear as a bell. "Before the sky goes evening red. Come on, Skiff."

They dashed the dewy grass, a blur toward the whispering woods. Murmurs grew with every step. Snippets rode the cool morning.

"Balloons… so many… bright and bouncy," a tiny red-cap, voice like a tinkling bell.

"Cake… rich chocolate… piled with sprinkles," a plump brown one, pleased as a bird.

The mushrooms were talking. Fern and Skiff ran faster.

Then the largest cluster, magnificent King Boletes, caps as grand as crowns, a booming joyful rumble: "SURPRISE. HAPPY BIRTHDAY, FARMER GILES."

Fern's hands found her mouth. "They are too loud."

"Muffle them," Skiff spun, gears a blur.

Her mind raced. Softest moss nearby. Enormous downy dandelion clocks, ready to send their seeds. Armfuls of both.

"Skiff. A hand."

They bounced and bundled. She tucked moss around the Boletes' bases until excited whispers softened to hums. Skiff's tin claws set fluffy clocks on the grand caps, cozy temporary hats. The boom went. A contented sigh rippled the whole patch. Whispers braided into a sweet secret song only the woods needed to hear.

They stood, a little puffed, wide grins. A puff of fluff tickled Fern's nose. Skiff clicked and whirred.

They listened. No shouts. A happy hum of kept secrets.

The sun took its slow dip. Down by the oak, Farmer Giles arrived. His eyes did the work of a surprise. A cheer went up that did not need mushrooms — people, cake, the day keeping its own counsel.

Fern heard it from the path, already moving, Skiff a bright clatter at her shoulder. The mushrooms were talking still, but softly now, under their dandelion hats, and the morning, which had begun with dew like coins, had somewhere else to be.
